name: Defias Brotherhood
summary: Across Stormwind’s southern lands, the Defias Brotherhood wages war on the kingdom. Bandits, brigands, and assassins terrorize the farmlands. From a hidden redoubt, they seek to overthrow the corrupt House of Nobles and lay waste to Stormwind.

sections.title: A Web of Conspiracies
sections.body:
Far beyond a band of displaced laborers, the Defias Brotherhood has spread its reach. VanCleef hired mercenary goblins to oversee armaments, joined forces with Riverpaw gnolls and Elwynn kobolds, and traded with cutthroat pirates such as the Bloodsail Buccaneers.

Highwaymen rob gold shipments across Elwynn Forest. Their agents gained a foothold in Duskwood, then uncovered a cursed artifact in Roland's Doom. Treacherous aristocrats in the House of Nobles secretly support them, and the Brotherhood arranges kidnappings aimed at the Alliance's highest offices.

sections.title: The Juggernaught in the Deadmines
sections.body:
Beneath Moonbrook, goblin engineers secretly build the Defias Juggernaught at Ironclad Cove. The iron-plated warship is a floating fortress, meant to sail through underground coastal waterways and bombard Stormwind City from the sea. Its guns would reduce the city's grand architecture to rubble.

The conspiracy reaches the royal court. Corrupt nobles such as Lord Gregor Lescovar act as eyes and ears for the uprising. Lady Katrana Prestor's court machinations keep the kingdom divided and blind to the fleet rising beneath Westfall.

sections.title: From Masons to Marauders
sections.body:
After the Second War, the Stonemasons Guild rebuilt Stormwind from smoldering ruins into a grand stone capital. When the work was done, the House of Nobles refused the promised payment, citing crushing wartime debt. Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef spoke for his workers and demanded fair restitution. The nobles ordered the guild disbanded. Riots followed, and the laborers were driven from Stormwind into exile.

Outlawed and stripped of their livelihood, VanCleef and the desperate workers banded together. They bound red silk around their faces for the blood of the wronged. Then they turned to highway robbery to claim what they believed they were owed.

sections.title: The Shadow Over Westfall
sections.body:
With the royal army stretched thin, VanCleef made Westfall's neglected farmlands the Brotherhood's base. The bandits seized Moonbrook and took over the abandoned tunnels beneath the Deadmines. Defias agents took local mines and drove farmers from their homes with reprogrammed harvest golems. They also salted the earth to starve the region.

The Crown could not or would not send soldiers to protect rural citizens. From Sentinel Hill, local farmers formed The People's Militia. Now they wage a desperate war of attrition against an enemy that outnumbers and outguns them.

faq.q: Why do the Defias wear red bandanas?
faq.answer: Edwin VanCleef and the exiled stonemasons wore red silk bandanas as a sign of defiance. The color recalls the blood shed by the workers who rebuilt Stormwind, then faced broken promises, violence, and exile from the nobility.

faq.q: Why is the Brotherhood attacking innocent farmers instead of nobles?
faq.answer: The Brotherhood began with real grievances against the nobility, but years of lawless exile turned it into a brutal criminal empire. Desperation, greed, and the arrival of ruthless cutthroats and goblins drove its members to pillage homesteads, burn crops, and seize mines to fund their war machine.

Edwin VanCleef was the brilliant guildmaster of the Stonemasons Guild, which rebuilt Stormwind City after the Second War. Skilled in stealth and subterfuge, he founded the Defias Brotherhood after the House of Nobles refused to pay the workers. He now directs its operations from deep within the Deadmines.

faq.q: Why doesn't Stormwind send the army to deal with the Defias?
faq.answer: The kingdom's coffers are drained, and the Stormwind Army is stretched thin guarding distant outposts such as those in Stranglethorn. Gridlock in the House of Nobles further paralyzes the throne, leaving rural Westfall and Duskwood to rely on volunteer militias.

The People's Militia is a volunteer defense force organized by Gryan Stoutmantle and the beleaguered farmers of Sentinel Hill. Stormwind has sent almost no soldiers to drive the Defias from Westfall, so local citizens took up arms to defend their land.

faq.q: What are the Defias building inside the Deadmines?
faq.answer: Goblin engineers and rogue artisans are building the Defias Juggernaught in Ironclad Cove, a hidden cavern beneath the earth. The massive iron-plated war galley is meant to sail into Stormwind Harbor and destroy the capital.

faq.q: Did the Defias have something to do with the King's disappearance?
faq.answer: What became of King Varian Wrynn remains a mystery. He vanished while traveling to a peace summit in Theramore, leaving the child Anduin on the throne under a regent.

angles.text: For humans of the kingdom, the Defias are a bitter reminder of rot within Stormwind. Aristocratic greed turned honest city builders into cutthroats.
The Knights of the Silver Hand and church leaders such as Duthorian Rall call on you to defend homesteaders like Daphne Stilwell from Defias brigands in Westfall.
Master Mathias Shaw and SI:7 watch the Defias closely. VanCleef's operatives rival royal scouts in lockpicking, stealth, and deadly ambushes beneath the earth.
The uprising threatens the kingdom's stability. It chokes Westfall's grain supplies, destabilizes gold mines, and shakes public faith in Stormwind's leadership.
